This is reported as a blocker per the task brief's explicit instruction ("if seams remain insufficient, report a concrete external production-seam blocker rather than hiding imports or expanding scope") rather than reintroducing the dynamic-import technique the reviewer already rejected.

items.root_cause: assistant/management_service.py's _bff_management_nl_ask_impl (called by POST /bff/management/nl/ask) resolves read_store and OpenClawOpsClient as module-level _DynamicProxy instances (management_service.py:1071-1163) whose __call__/__getattr__ resolve via _resolve_main() -> sys.modules.get('services.control_plane.bff.main') (management_service.py:1067-1068). Unlike the conversation store (which has a real set_management_ai_conversation_store/get_management_ai_conversation_store DI seam), there is no injectable parameter or real setter for read_store or OpenClawOpsClient anywhere in management_service.py or its callers. The only way to make these resolve to a test double is for services.control_plane.bff.main to already be present in sys.modules -- which requires either importing the real main.py (rejected by the reviewer as a hidden/dynamic main import) or registering a fabricated stand-in module at that exact sys.modules key (which would still leave every other test file executed in the same interpreter process reading a fake main.py, an unacceptable cross-test-file side effect in a shared pytest session).
items.required_production_change: assistant/management_service.py needs a real, explicit DI seam for read_store and OpenClawOpsClient (an injectable parameter or a set_*/get_* pair analogous to set_management_ai_conversation_store), removing the _DynamicProxy/_resolve_main() dependency on sys.modules for these two names.
items.additional_defect_observed: Independent of the import mechanism, these 4 tests also fail with a RecursionError raised from _DynamicProxy.__getattr__ during copy.deepcopy() of a Management NL command-idempotency result, even when main.py is loaded and the dynamic proxy successfully resolves. This means the prior generation's rejected importlib.import_module() workaround did not actually make these 4 tests pass either -- it only hid the AC2 violation from the AST scanner while the tests kept failing for an unrelated reason. Root cause not further investigated (out of scope: fixing it requires editing assistant/management_service.py, production source).

The startup command-replay test inherently needs main.py's own process-global state and cannot be seamed away without changing what the test proves.
